title: Submit, inspect, and cancel Nucleus jobs
summary: Admit an exact request, observe its single attempt and global execution capacity, wait for runtime state, or cancel one job.
use_when: An exact runtime request must be submitted, inspected, awaited, or cancelled.
Queueing, execution capacity, timeout, terminal state, or restart loss must be interpreted.
do_not_use_when: The actual goal is a requester-owned domain result or a decision to retry domain work.
Ordinary interactive agent work does not require a Nucleus job merely because it uses a model.
outcome: An exact job is admitted or its current runtime state or cancellation is observed.
effects: Submission creates a durable job and one attempt and may invoke Codex and consume account allowance.
Cancellation records durable intent for one exact job; reads expose retained runtime state.
authority: Nucleus owns admission, the global eight-slot scheduler, one attempt per job, runtime lifecycle, and cancellation.
Requesters own domain records, success, conflicting writes, and whether another attempt is safe.
success: Submission admits the exact request under its chosen ID, or a supported read confirms the selected job state.
Requester-owned evidence is inspected separately whenever domain success matters.
failure_and_recovery: Repeat uncertain submission only with the same job ID and byte-equivalent typed request.
Inspect domain state after failure, timeout, loss, or quota exhaustion before authorizing a new job.
privacy: Nucleus private state can contain complete prompts, source content, tool arguments and results, exact harness output, and terminal diagnostics. Keep state and logs private.
does_not_authorize: Requester-domain acceptance or a new attempt after failure or loss.
Service restart while active attempts must remain uninterrupted.

consumers.statement: Local applications and the current user may submit exact version-one jobs and observe or cancel their attempts.

preconditions.statement: Admission requires a compatible daemon, exact supported harness and invocation policy, ready authentication, and applicable admission conditions; a free execution slot is not required.
The requester persists its exact request and domain-run correlation and decides that a new attempt is safe.

inputs.statement: A version-one request includes a requester-chosen job ID, label, requester program and ID, instructions, prompt, and a closed invocation policy; optional developer instructions and parent provenance retain their documented roles.
Inspection and cancellation select exact job IDs; listing can select requester program and domain-run ID.
No workflow graph, automatic-retry policy, or requester-domain mutation is accepted.

outputs.statement: Submission, job show, list, status, wait, and cancellation return version-one runtime observations. Status includes attempt identity/state, pending calls, output availability, and terminal reason/message.
Nucleus returns no requester-domain success assertion or automatic replacement attempt.

data_semantics.statement: A job is the durable admitted request with one attempt. Accepted jobs have pending attempts until a slot is available; waiting_on_requester still occupies a slot.
Terminal state describes runtime execution, not application success. A wait-command timeout is an observation and does not cancel the job.

identity_and_units.statement: Job ID is the request idempotency key; requester program plus requester ID identifies the domain run; attempt ID identifies the single execution.
The service has eight global active slots. Invocation timeoutSeconds is wall-clock seconds starting after slot acquisition and includes requester-tool waiting.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Reads describe committed local state at their read boundary. Status reads job and mailbox state in sequence, not as an atomic snapshot; list defaults to 20 and preserves continuation.
No job-start, completion, or service-availability objective is promised.

access.statement: The supported standard surfaces are the current-user CLI and version-one HTTP protocol over Nucleus's filesystem-protected Unix socket.
Local filesystem ownership and permissions protect the socket and private state; version one has no application-level authentication protocol.
No TCP endpoint, cross-user service, catalog-granted access, or direct SQLite integration is supported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Byte-equivalent resubmission under one ID returns the existing job; changed content conflicts. Cancellation is durable and idempotent, including when it overlaps startup.

Queued cancellation does not start Codex. Cancellation cannot erase history or undo committed requester effects. Startup marks every unfinished attempt lost, including pending attempts; Nucleus never retries automatically.
Quota deferral creates no new job; admitted main-Codex jobs can wait for quota without a slot or running timeout. Maintenance holds permit admitted work to settle.

operational_limits.statement: Version one allows one attempt per job and at most eight active attempts, including requester waits through terminal cleanup. Nucleus does not coordinate write conflicts or interpret workflows.
Beyond the eight-active-attempt ceiling, no throughput, queue-depth, database-capacity, output-volume, retention, or wall-clock-latency bound is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: The job and HTTP envelopes remain version one while invocation policies one and two are supported. Public protocol, store, adapter, exact harness, feature contract, and provider release evolve independently.
No general requester-support window or deprecation interval is promised.

reliances.statement: Execution relies on the separately installed exact adapter-proved Codex runtime and its account service; no installed Chancery contract covers that external behavior.
